Let \(R=\mathbb Z/2^m\mathbb Z\). Write
\[
A=\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{pmatrix},\qquad s=a+d.
\]
Then \(A^2=0\) is equivalent to
\[
sb=0,\qquad sc=0,\qquad a^2+bc=0,\qquad d^2+bc=0.
\]
Since \(d=s-a\), the last two quadratic equations are equivalent to
\[
a^2+bc=0,\qquad s(s-2a)=0.
\]

First count the trace-zero case \(s=0\). Then \(d=-a\), and we need
\[
bc=-a^2.
\]
Let \(N_n\) be the number of triples \((a,b,c)\in(\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z)^3\) with \(bc=-a^2\), and set \(N_0=1\). For \(n\ge1\), if \(x\in\mathbb Z/2^n\mathbb Z\) has valuation \(k<n\), the number of pairs \((b,c)\) with \(bc=x\) is \((k+1)2^{n-1}\). If \(x=0\), it is \((n+2)2^{n-1}\). Summing over \(v_2(a)\) gives
\[
N_{2q}=3\cdot 2^{4q-1}-2^{3q-1},
\]
and
\[
N_{2q+1}=6\cdot 2^{4q}-2^{3q+1}.
\]

Now take \(s\neq0\), with \(v_2(s)=v\), and put \(r=m-v\). Then \(sb=sc=0\) forces
\[
b,c\in 2^rR.
\]
The equation \(s(s-2a)=0\) is equivalent to
\[
2a\equiv s\pmod {2^r}.
\]
There are no solutions unless \(v\ge r\), i.e. \(r\le \lfloor m/2\rfloor\). For such \(r\), write
\[
a=2^{r-1}y,\qquad b=2^rB,\qquad c=2^rC.
\]
Then
\[
a^2+bc\equiv0\pmod{2^m}
\]
reduces exactly to
\[
y^2+4BC\equiv0\pmod {2^{m-2r+2}}.
\]
Writing \(y=2Y\), this becomes
\[
Y^2+BC\equiv0\pmod {2^{m-2r}},
\]
so for each fixed \(s\) of valuation \(m-r\), the number of matrices is
\[
2^{3r}N_{m-2r}.
\]
There are \(2^{r-1}\) choices of such \(s\). Therefore the total number is
\[
N_m+\sum_{r=1}^{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}2^{4r-1}N_{m-2r}.
\]

Substituting the formulas for \(N_n\) and simplifying gives
\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
(3m+8)2^{2m-3}, & m\ \text{even},\\[2mm]
(3m+5)2^{2m-3}, & m\ \text{odd}.
\end{cases}}
\]
